fields.statement: QA cycle 2, hands-on with a binary built from the branch head, in a scratch repo with a fake rex and a three-question transcript (Which colour?/Which store?/Which port?). The change set held a Decision with question 'Which port?' verbatim and one with 'which colour?' (case differs). rhiza session done printed 'Proposed decision answer-<sid8>-1', '-2' and 'Skipped answer-<sid8>-3: already recorded'; only answer-1 and answer-2 were written. In a second change set, with 'Which store?' recorded and a retired 'Which colour?' Decision, session done --json returned decisions [answer-<sid8>-1, answer-<sid8>-3] and skipped [answer-<sid8>-2]; answer-1 carries question 'Which colour?' and the owner-pick wording. A repeat session done returned already:true and proposed nothing. go test TestScripts/session-interview-recorded and describe-golden pass.

QA cycle 2: ran rhiza guide plan from a binary built at the branch head. It says the run's capture records the owner's AskUserQuestion picks and the planner writes no Decision for a plain owner pick; the planner writes one only when the capture's wording would be wrong (a proxy such as an orchestrator or arbiter answered, or a ruling the capture cannot word), with the proxy's wording and the asked question copied verbatim into question so the capture skips it. No line tells the planner to write Decisions for plain picks.
